timeline.label: Q2 2026 results: revenue $504M (+75% YoY) and diluted EPS $1.65 signal cycle rebound from FY2025 trough
Federal coal lease renewals for Mine No. 1 and Mine No. 4 filed; supports reserve continuity
FY2025 10-K: trough year with $57M net income, $229M operating cash flow, 9.3M metric tons produced
S-3ASR shelf registration filed for potential equity/debt offerings
FY2024 earnings decline begins: revenue $1.50B, net income $251M as met coal prices soften
Post-strike operations normalized; FY2022–2023 represented peak cycle earnings (net income up to $479M in 2023)
United Mine Workers strike ended; operations restart at Alabama longwall mines after 13-month stoppage
UMWA strike begins at Warrior Met mines over contract terms; production halted
Warrior Met Coal IPO completed (NYSE: HCC) after emerging from Walter Energy bankruptcy estate
Operations acquired from Walter Energy bankruptcy; company formed as pure-play met coal producer

industry.structure: Global seaborne metallurgical coal is an oligopoly of large low-cost mines plus marginal producers; pricing is spot and index-linked with high cyclicality. U.S. Gulf Coast exports compete with Australia and Canada on quality and freight.
industry.share_shift: Warrior holds premium Blue Creek-type reserves in Alabama; share gains depend on longwall uptime and port/rail access rather than greenfield discovery among U.S. peers.
industry.trend: 2025 was a pricing trough for met coal after 2022–2023 peaks; 2026 H1 rebound tracks steel demand and supply disruptions. Blue Creek development and Section 45X critical-mineral credits for met coal (OBBBA, 10-K FY2025) are current industry policy tailwinds.
